subject: Post-call recap: discovery gaps, success metrics & onramp checklist for Novaside POC
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaside.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: discovery gaps, success metrics & onramp checklist for Novaside POC

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC standing up next week. Please let me know if I missed or mis-stated anything.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Production spikes when running batch enrichment jobs (90th pct latency spikes to 1.2s) causing downstream request timeouts.
- Current cost per inference for the embedding+rerank flow is high and inconsistent across peaks.
- Need to preserve PII controls and auditability for requests originating from EU customers.

Primary POC goals (mutually agreed):
1) Reduce 90th percentile inference latency for search rerank from ~1.2s to <=350ms for 95% of traffic.
2) Demonstrate a 25% reduction in per-request token cost measured on your representative workload.
3) Validate prefix caching + minimal quantization profile without impacting rerank quality (precision@10 target within 2% of baseline).

Proposed scope and owners:
- Redwood deliverables: POC charter & baseline eval harness, hosted sandbox with traffic shaping, recommended quantization profile, and a short prompt/eval suite. (Owner: Hannah)
- Novaside deliverables: sample prompt set (200 queries + ground-truth ranking), S3 access for logs, and test traffic window (staging API key). (Owner: Alex / Platform team)
- Technical leads: Ben (Redwood AE/infra lead) will coordinate runtime tuning; Marissa (CS) will own quality regressions and evals.

Access & setup checklist (what we need from Novaside to start):
1) Sandbox API key (scoped) – send to redwood-sandbox@redwood.ai via secure channel or DocuSign.
2) Temporary S3 read/write role for logs: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/novaside-poc-readonly (or an equivalent bucket + presigned access).
3) Allowlist of staging IPs for the sandbox (we will provide the CIDR block).
4) A short document with the production traffic profile (qps, typical prompt lengths).

Timeline (proposed):
- Wed (11/11): Exchange access & confirm S3/keys.
- Thu–Fri (11/12–11/13): Baseline runs + one tuning pass.
- Mon (11/16): Present baseline vs tuned results, recommend quantization profile and batching parameters.

Attachments: I attached a first draft of the POC charter and an access checklist.

Next steps (for this week):
- Alex: Share sample prompt set and S3 location by EOD Tue.
- Ben: I will send the sandbox CIDR and onboarding instructions by tomorrow.
- Marissa: I’ll coordinate the eval rubric and send a shared Drive folder for results.

Thanks again — excited to get this rolling.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment(s): novaside-poc-charter-v1.docx, access-instructions.md

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaside.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Novaside Platform <platform@novaside.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: discovery gaps, success metrics & onramp checklist for Novaside POC

Thanks Hannah — this is great and matches our notes. A couple clarifications from the platform team: 

- Priority SLA: target median latency under 250ms and 95th under 500ms for the rerank path. We recognize the 90th/95th framing but wanted to call out tighter internal goals.
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 evidence and an encrypted log pipeline. Can Redwood confirm support for SSE-KMS on exported logs and a contact for SOC2 documentation?
- Traffic window: best to run baseline during our lower traffic period (01:00–03:00 UTC) to avoid affecting production customers.

I'll upload the sample prompt set to the Drive link and grant your service account read access by EOD today. Expect S3 details and the staging key tomorrow morning.

—
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering | Novaside
alex.rivera@novaside.com

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 3:12 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC standing up next week. Please let me know if I missed or mis-stated anything.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaside.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: discovery gaps, success metrics & onramp checklist for Novaside POC

Adding a few technical notes and a condensed action list from the infra side: 

- We will spin up a sandbox instance with the same model family you use (Llama2-70B equivalent) and apply two quantization profiles: 8-bit server-friendly and a more aggressive 4-bit for cost testing.
- Batching policy: start with max-batch-size=32 and dynamic batching windows tuned to the submitted traffic profile.
- Observability: we will push request-level traces and a small set of KPI dashboards (latency p50/p95, tokens per request, failed requests).

Action items (technical):
1) Alex: Confirm the production model family and provide a small set (5–10) of representative longer prompts for eval.
2) Alex: Grant the redwood-poc role read access to the S3 bucket or provide presigned URLs.
3) Hannah/Ben: Provision sandbox and share connection details + allowlist CIDRs by Wed EOD (11/11).

If we hit the latency targets on the tuned profile, we will capture cost delta and a short report for the Novaside execs. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the dashboard once we have the baseline.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: discovery gaps, success metrics & onramp checklist for Novaside POC

Alex — appreciate the clarifications. Quick updates and confirmations: 

- SOC 2 / Compliance: Marissa will be your SOC2 point of contact and will share the SOC2 package and our KMS integration notes by EOD today. (Marissa: can you attach the compliance one-pager and the KMS flow?)
- SSE-KMS: Confirmed — we support SSE-KMS for exported logs; will document the required role policy in the access-instructions.md attachment.
- Sandbox timing: Ben and I will schedule the baseline run for 01:30–02:30 UTC on Thu (11/12) per your low-traffic window. If anything changes on your side let us know.

Checklist update and immediate asks: 
- Alex: Upload prompt set to Drive and grant redwood-poc@redwood.ai read access (we received the first batch, thanks).
- Novaside Platform: Please provision the S3 role or send presigned bucket URLs by tomorrow morning (11/13) so we can instrument logging.
- Marissa: attaching the compliance packet (SOC2 summary) and the access-instructions doc for your team.

I'll schedule a 30-min touchpoint after the baseline run for a quick readout and to agree on the tuning pass.

Best —
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
